findings.reason: the node would install the claim guard on the prediction path only; the real `crew resume`/dispatch launcher and the process that must acquire the claim are both outside the named mechanism, so the defect §4 exists to close stays open on the production path.
findings.text: §4 says "A held claim refuses the launch" and names the guard as `_launcher_refusal` in `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, but that function is only the sweep's prediction mirror (called once, at `resumption.py:1294`); the real launcher guard is `resume_plan` in `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:995`, which already duplicates this guard and the docstring at `resumption.py:593` holds the two in parity ("`resume_plan` and this function must refuse the same record with the same message"), enforced by `tests/test_dry_run_predicts_the_launcher.py:180-183`. §4 grants write paths only `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, `reckon/crew/runs.py` and the new test, and names no caller for the claim's acquisition ("A launched worker holds a claim on its worker session for its lifetime" — nothing says who writes it). A builder following §4 literally edits the mirror, not the real launch path, and the parity test would then either fail or the production resume would be admitted.

findings.reason: as written the plan's driving followup misroutes the second guard to §3 and provides no invocation for §4, so §4's live-session claim can be dropped without any followup appearing unresolved.
findings.text: the only open followup `f-arolw-002` recommends `/reckon-build a-run-has-one-live-worker §3` and its body says "§3 repairs the two guards §2 named, with a test reproducing each", but §3's deliverable and done-when cover only the once-only lift (one test, `tests/test_a_hold_lifts_once.py`); the second guard is §4, which carries no followup at all. A coordinator closing §3's followup would believe both guards landed and leave §4 unbuilt.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/resumption.py` (`sweep`, `_launcher_refusal`, `_stamp_resumption_trigger`), `reckon/crew/runs.py` (`record_process_alive`), the §2 report, the `a-run-has-one-live-worker-landed.html#s2-second-launcher` archive (the `s2-second-launcher` id exists) and the `a-crew-process-ends-with-its-owner` dependency all resolve; §3's "recovery log lines 7668 and 7669" names a line without naming its file, but the §2 report it cites names `~/.config/reckon/crew/recovery/nova.jsonl`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §3 ("the test fails on the current code") and §4 ("the first case is admitted on the current code and the test fails") each name an executed negative control, and §4 declares both the refusing and the admitting arm.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-whens log the negative control to the run's record beside the run; no scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4's stated root cause and §3's both match the §2 report, but §4 names `_launcher_refusal` (the sweep's prediction mirror) as "the launch path" and scopes writes away from the real launcher, so the repaired guard would not run on the production resume call.
